text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Civil servants unions demand wage increase above inflation. (p1)
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo does not believe in secret understanding between France and Germany to appoint Frenchman as first president of European Central Bank. (ECB).
- Philips Electronics closes loss-giving video shop chain Superclub after failing to find buyer. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell and retailer Ahold step up plans for Albert Heijn supermarkets at Shell filling stations. (p1)
- Amsterdam court rules against holders of bonds in former truckmaker DAF, who claim Dfl 150 million in guarantees. (p1)
- U.S. maker of chips industry machines accuses rival ASM International of breach of patent. (p3)
- Wholesaler Sligro books 13.3 pct higher 1996 EPS at Dfl 6.03. (p3)
- Factory gate prices of Dutch industry in November are 0.7 pct down from month before.
VOLKSKRANT
- ABN Amro staffing policy unleashes row in City of London. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airines/KLM wins court case against partner Northwest Airlines. (p2)
- Shorter working week at ABN Amro bank produced 1,000 new jobs in 1996. (p2)
- Schiphol Airport wants charters to fly from regional airports. (p31)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Large number of rules are no hindrance for labour market, says research institute OSA. (p31)
- Florishing airline Air Holland to expand fleet. (p31)
- DAF Trucks sells 800 less trucks in 1996 than 1995, expects fierce competition. (p33)
- Dutch market for interim-managment growing 15-20 pct per year. (p33)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch dispatching agents owe about one billion guilders in customs' duties. (p10)
- Economic affairs minister of Germany's North-Rhine Westphalia criticises Netherlands for giving foreign investors tax advantages. (p13)
TROUW
- KLM to replace paper flying tickets with electronic counterparts. (p7) A
